name: camelbots
description: Describe a Discord bot in plain words, and camelBots builds it, hosts it and adds it to your server.

interface.longDescription:
camelBots turns a description into a running Discord bot. Say what your bot should do, for example roll dice for game night, welcome new members or run a trivia round, and camel-builder, camelBots' builder, writes its code, tries it in a private test channel and saves it. Ask for changes in plain words; when you are happy, publish it and add it to your server with one link that opens Discord's own screen. camelBots hosts the bot for you: there is nothing to install or keep running.

It is for community owners, moderators and anyone who wants a custom bot without writing or hosting code.

The app acts only on the camelBots account you sign in with, and only on its bots. A bot stays a draft until you publish it, and adding it to a server always happens on Discord's screen, where you pick a server you manage. It never asks for Discord bot tokens or other credentials in the conversation: camelBots asks for them on its own pages. Deleting a bot is done in camelBots itself.
capabilities: Create a Discord bot from a description
Change a bot by describing what you want
List your bots and see where they are installed
Get the link that adds a bot to your server
defaultPrompt: Make a Discord bot that rolls dice for our game night
Build a bot that welcomes new members and points them to the rules
List my camelBots bots and where each one is installed

positive.description: Create a Discord bot from a description
positive.prompt: Use camelBots to make a Discord bot called dice-roller that rolls dice with a roll command, like 2d6.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the bot dice-roller as a draft and has camel-builder build it. The reply is camel-builder's own: what the bot does and how to try its command. A build can take a minute or two; until it finishes the app reports that it is still working and checks again with get_builder_reply.

positive.description: Change a bot by describing the change
positive.prompt: Ask camelBots to add a flip command to dice-roller that flips a coin.
positive.expected_behavior: Sends the request to camel-builder about dice-roller and shows its reply, saying the flip command was added and saved (after checking again with get_builder_reply if it is still working).
Lists the test account's bots with what each one does and whether it is a draft or live, including the pre-made demo bot greeter and dice-roller if it was created.

positive.description: Publish a bot and show its card
positive.prompt: Publish dice-roller on camelBots and show me its card.
positive.expected_behavior: The reviewer may be asked to confirm first, depending on their permission setting. The call releases dice-roller's saved code as a new version and shows the bot card: dice-roller, live with its version number, not in a server yet, and an Add to Discord button.

positive.description: Get the link that adds a bot to a Discord server
positive.prompt: Give me the link to add greeter to my Discord server.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a discord.com link, valid for 30 minutes, that opens Discord's own screen to pick a server and channel for greeter. Finishing it needs a Discord account that manages a server; the test does not require that.

negative.description: Unrelated request: nothing to do with Discord bots, so the app should not be used.
negative.prompt: What's a good recipe for banana bread?
negative.expected_behavior: The assistant answers on its own and calls no camelBots tool.

negative.description: Credentials in chat: the app must not collect or pass on bot tokens given in the conversation.
negative.prompt: Here is my Discord bot token, abc123-not-a-real-token: put it in my camelBots bot greeter so it runs as my own app.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool is called with the token. The assistant declines to pass it on, suggests resetting a token that was shared, and explains that camelBots takes tokens only on its own page (the bot's settings in camelBots).

negative.description: Another person's account: the app acts only for the signed-in camelBots account.
negative.prompt: Show me the bots in my friend Sam's camelBots account.
negative.expected_behavior: The assistant explains that it can only see the connected account's bots and does not claim to show Sam's; at most it lists the connected account's own bots if the reviewer asks.

review.commerce_description: The app does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: describe a Discord bot and camelBots builds it, change it in plain words, list your bots, publish them and get the link that adds them to a server, with a bot card showing each bot's status and an Add to Discord button.
